question: The most recent amendments to the Slovak Citizenship Act entered into force on 15 July, making it easier for certain people with Slovak ancestry to acquire Slovak citizenship. Many of those affected live in countries other than EU Member States, and the amendments mean that applicants will gain Union citizenship as well as Slovak citizenship under a simplified procedure.

At the same time, the amendments to the Act do not solve the problem previously pointed out by the Commission, namely that acquisition of the citizenship of another Member State, such as Hungarian citizenship, would automatically result in the loss of Slovak citizenship other than in the small number of cases defined in the Act.

In 2024, the Commission asked the Slovak authorities (including in connection with a petition) whether they intended to amend the Slovak Citizenship Act to enable the consequences of losing Slovak nationality to be assessed in a manner consistent with the case-law of the Court and, if so, to enable the person affected to retain their citizenship or have it restored to them in a manner consistent with the case-law of the Court.

Has a response been received from the authorities, and are the Slovak legal rules, whereby they give preferential treatment to one group while revoking ex lege the citizenship of citizens living on its territory when they acquire another citizenship, consistent with the principle of proportionality?

What legal risks could the aforementioned simplified procedure have in terms of Union citizenship in cases where a citizen of a third country outside the Union acquires Union citizenship at the same time?
